deploy.$comment: boot.py seeds the stores and then execs the API — it is not a wrapper that can be skipped. A startCommand of `python -m core.api.app` boots an API over an empty volume, because Kuzu is single-writer and the API holds the lock.
deploy.$timeout_comment: 1800s, cut from 14400 on 2026-08-13, and the cut IS the fix rather than a tuning of it. The old window was sized to let the boot LOAD THE ARCHIVE before binding — ~1.33M wire events merged into Kuzu at ~145 events/sec (slower as the graph grows), plus an un-resumable archive-wide rescore wanting hours more. That arithmetic was correct and the objective was wrong: because Kuzu is single-writer, every second of it is a second the site is DARK, so a four-hour ceiling bought a four-hour outage for work that was not urgent. The reasoning that produced it — 'a window too short kills a container that was working' — is true and was over-applied: a long window is not free, it just moves the cost from a dead container to a dark one. Bulk loading (GEOGRAPH_GDELT_ON_BOOT) and the rescore (GEOGRAPH_RESCORE_ON_BOOT) are now opt-in jobs, and the event study is metered by GEOGRAPH_STUDY_BUDGET instead of taking the remainder, because its per-event watermark makes progress fungible across boots while downtime is not. What is left before the API binds is seeding, a cached deep tier, 13F flows and a bounded study: minutes. 1800 is the ceiling on that, not the target — boot.py's _WINDOW_SECONDS must equal this number and test_the_boot_window_matches_railway_json enforces it. Raise BOTH together, and only for a deploy whose job is loading.
